newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala expects $800 million in post-war aid.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala expects $800 million in post-war aid.

text.p: Guatemala expects industrialized nations to loan and donate $800 million for peacetime development projects as the country seeks to rebuild after a long civil war, the central bank said Thursday.
"It's realistic to hope for $800 million in loans and foreign aid to be released over the next three years," Willy Zapata, president of the Banco de Guatemala, told reporters at a news conference.
Guatemala is six weeks away from the signing of a peace agreement between the government and leftist guerrillas to end a 36-year conflict.

The government is seeking a total of $1.5 billion in foreign aid, loans and investment to implement promises contained in peace accords to improve the country's health, education and judicial systems.
The Interamerican Development Bank announced Wednesday it would loan Guatemala $50 million for rural development programs in a war-torn area in the northwestern highlands.
Zapata said the Economy Ministry and the bank are preparing to meet with a consulting group of donor countries organized by the Interamerican Development Bank in Brussels January 21-22.
The group, including delegates from Norway, Sweden, Japan, France and the United States, will decide how much each country would contribute.
Zapata said $800 million was a realistic amount to expect from the consulting group, but Guatemala could receive more than that because of the great need in rural areas torn apart during the war.
Donor countries are likely to seek assurances that Guatemala is improving tax collection and increasing its low tax burden to help finance its own projects.

Zapata said the bank met Wednesday with representatives from the Guatemalan embassies of donor nations to report on advances in the preparation of projects. Guatemalan officials will visit several European countries before the end of the year to present proposals on development projects.
